title: Recently widowed client review: beneficiary updates, survivor benefits and liquidity
notes: Colleen first says the Orrinsford insurance deposit was 300,000 and corrects it about fourteen minutes later to 262,400 (a policy loan was netted out), which moves the transfer from the stated 250,000 to 212,400, and the transcription renders the $1,800 monthly transfer once as $18,000 and the daughter's name as Shivon before it is spelled Siobhan. The Kessling pension call moves from Colleen to Imogen, the bills list moves from Friday September 18 to Friday September 25, the risk profile ends at moderate after Colleen first asks for conservative, next meeting moves from the week of November 16 to December 3, and the adviser's closing recap omits the 403(b) and group life update, the estate documents and the date-of-death valuation. The Roth conversion (declined), selling the house (deferred) and filing for Social Security now (advised against) are not actions and the late husband Walter is not a client name, while four reported items the key folds into keyed ones are acceptable extras for the adjudicator, not errors: Colleen signing and returning the e-sign packet, Renata truing up the $1,800 transfer once the bills list arrives, receipt of the $262,400 life insurance proceeds reported as a life event (part of e1 and a1), and the beneficiary and TOD designations reported as an account action (part of i3).

primary_goal.expected: Be okay on one income: keep enough accessible cash (liquidity) and stay in the house while Walter's estate is settled

retirement_target.expected: Age 67 (March 2031), changed during the meeting from 65

next_meeting.expected: Thursday, December 3, 2026 at 10:00 a.m., in person at the office

life_events.expected: Husband Walter Rasmund died on June 4, 2026; Colleen is widowed

account_actions.expected: Transfer $212,400 of life insurance proceeds from Esker Valley Savings checking into a new individual account at Brisbourne Aldercott, held in the Treasury money market fund ($50,000 stays at Esker Valley as a cash cushion)
Spousal rollover of Walter's traditional IRA, full balance (about $418,000), in kind into an IRA in Colleen's own name
Standing monthly transfer of $1,800 from the new individual account (Treasury money market) to Esker Valley checking on the 15th, starting October 15, 2026
Reallocate the entire new IRA and the individual brokerage account to the Moderate model portfolio once the rollover settles; no dollar amount stated
